title: U.S. House · California's 20th Congressional District
area: Kern County, including most of Bakersfield, and parts of Tulare and Kings counties in the southern San Joaquin Valley.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election.
In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Vince Fong won 68.2% of the vote (115,035 votes) and Sandra Van Scotter won 28.8% (48,611 votes), advancing them both to the November general election.

candidates.name: Vince Fong
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 20th District (since June 2024, elected in a special election)

summary.text: Vince Fong is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for California's 20th District, a Bakersfield native who worked for Reps. Bill Thomas and Kevin McCarthy before serving in the California State Assembly from 2017 to 2024. He won a May 2024 special election to succeed McCarthy and was elected to a full term that November.

background.text: Born in Bakersfield, California, in 1979. Wikipedia reports that his parents were Chinese immigrants and that he attended West High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from UCLA in 2001 and a master's degree in public administration from Princeton University in 2003.

According to his official biography, he began his career with Rep. Bill Thomas, then chair of the House Ways and Means Committee, working on international trade policy, and later spent nearly a decade as district director to Rep. Kevin McCarthy in Kern County.

His official biography says he helped organize a Valley Fever Symposium to draw national attention to the disease, and Wikipedia lists service on the boards of Goodwill Industries of South Central California, the Jim Burke Education Foundation and Honor Flight Kern County.

Elected to the California State Assembly in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020 and 2022, representing Bakersfield-area districts. Bills he authored include measures on catalytic converter theft and wildfire prevention through controlled grazing; he resigned his seat on May 24, 2024.

After McCarthy resigned from Congress effective December 31, 2023, Fong ran in the special election, advanced to a runoff against Tulare County Sheriff Mike Boudreaux, and won the May 21, 2024 runoff, 60 percent to 39 percent. He was sworn in on June 3, 2024, and won a full term in November 2024.

Serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure, Science, Space, and Technology, and Homeland Security committees, and is a member of the Republican Study Committee, Western Caucus and Congressional Valley Fever Task Force, among other caucuses.
According to his official biography, he is a lifelong Kern County resident who lives in Bakersfield with his wife, Amanda.

priorities.text: Lists restoring California's oil and gas production and cutting energy regulation as a priority, describing it as key to lowering costs and strengthening national security.
Lists cutting regulatory barriers to housing construction and expanding housing supply as a priority for lowering home prices in the Central Valley.

positions.summary: Supports cutting regulatory barriers and streamlining permitting to expand housing supply.
positions.quote: Building more houses, cutting red tape, empowering local and rural lenders, and modernizing outdated federal programs is exactly how we lower costs and make housing more affordable.

positions.summary: Supported making the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act permanent rather than allowing its rates to expire, describing the expiration as the largest tax increase in American history.
positions.quote: This legislation delivers for the Central Valley by preventing the largest tax increase in American history, supporting our farmers and small businesses, and ensuring the sustainability of our government's fiscal future.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials; Water Resources and Environment subcommittees) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress.
Introduced H.J. Res. 210, a Congressional Review Act resolution to overturn the EPA's authorization of California's Air Resources Board At-Berth Regulation; the House passed it.

candidates.name: Sandra Van Scotter
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 28.8% of the vote

summary.text: Sandra Van Scotter is the Democratic nominee in California's 20th District, a health care worker and, as local news describes her, a longtime advocate for disability rights and veterans' issues. She finished second in the June 2026 primary, and her campaign emphasizes Medicare for All and streamlining disability benefits.

background.text: According to BallotReady, she worked as a respiratory therapist at Sarah Bush Lincoln (2004-2011) and Northwestern Memorial Hospital (2011-2014), in cardiac testing at Ridgecrest Regional Hospital (2017-2021), and as a direct support professional.
The Loop Newspaper in Tehachapi describes her as a longtime advocate for disability rights and veterans' issues.

In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she says her whole career has been advocating for people in places where they cannot speak for themselves, names Medicare for All as a key message, and lists streamlining veterans' and Social Security disability benefits as a policy passion.

Advanced from the June 2, 2026 primary with 28.8 percent of the vote, second to Fong's 68.2 percent, and was endorsed by the Tehachapi Mountain Democratic Club. The Loop reported in April that she had traveled more than 20,000 miles within the district.

priorities.text: Supports Medicare for All, citing S. 1560 (introduced April 2025) as a model for transitioning over four years from the current commercial-insurance system to a single-payer option.
Says she would prioritize collaborating with state, county, and local officials on agriculture, water, and housing-affordability issues affecting the district.
Says she is passionate about streamlining access to Veterans Disability Benefits, Social Security Disability Benefits, and Developmental Disability benefits.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All, describing commercial health insurance as treating premiums as a 'bottomless cup' of profit.
positions.quote: Medicare For All is the answer to getting our Health Care System on track.
